name: Rocky Mountain Rangelands Program
summary: Grants for voluntary habitat work in the Intermountain West: sagebrush rangeland restoration, secure ungulate migration corridors, and wetland bird and native fish habitat.

geography.label: Intermountain West (Idaho, Utah and neighbouring states)

reporting: Grantees report on project metrics chosen from the programme's list in NFWF's Easygrants system.

eligibility.rule: Is a nonprofit 501(c) organisation, government agency, Tribal government or educational institution
Is not a for-profit entity or an unincorporated individual
Does not use NFWF funds for ongoing legal-compliance efforts
Project directly and measurably contributes to one or more program goals

documents: Board of Trustees or Directors list, or statement that none exists

status.quote: Rocky Mountain Rangelands 2025 Request for Proposals - CLOSED

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date Thursday August 7, 2025, 11:59 PM ET

pool.quote: The Rocky Mountain Rangelands Program will award approximately $5 million.

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, U.S. Federal government agencies, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments, educational institutions.

geography.quote: NFWF will consider projects in Idaho that apply integrated, ecologically-based invasive plant management strategies

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

reporting.quote: the Rocky Mountain Rangelands Program has a list of metrics in Easygrants for full proposal applicants to choose from for future reporting

effort.quote: Full Proposal Due Date Thursday August 7, 2025, 11:59 PM ET

eligibility.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, U.S. Federal government agencies, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments, educational institutions.
Ineligible applicants include for-profit entities and unincorporated individuals.
NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation, and settlement agreements.
Proposals must specifically address how projects for which funds are requested will directly and measurably contribute to the accomplishment of one or more program goals.

after_award.quote: the Rocky Mountain Rangelands Program has a list of metrics in Easygrants for full proposal applicants to choose from for future reporting
